# ESD-2006-03-18-1: Nicholas "Nic" Harbison — Spring Lake, DeSoto MO

## Summary

On March 18, 2006, Nicholas "Nic" Harbison, 16, a sophomore basketball player at DeSoto High School, was electrocuted while swimming near a private dock in Spring Lake (Summerset Lake subdivision), Jefferson County, Missouri. Three companions were also in the water: Morgan Milfeld (15) and Timothy Fitzpatrick (15) were rendered unconscious and airlifted to St. John's Mercy Medical Center; a fourth teenager was present but not seriously injured.

Post-incident investigation revealed 10 amps of current flowing in the dock's supply cable and 4-6 VAC measured just 2 feet from the swim ladder. A chain leading into the water showed evidence of arcing, and a dead muskrat and ten dead minnows were found at the water's edge. The root cause was a defective or missing neutral conductor on a nearby AmerenUE 7,200V underground power distribution cable, which caused neutral return current to flow through the earth and concentrate at the bonded dock ladder.

## Legal Outcome

In 2009, a Jefferson County civil jury returned a **$2.3 million verdict** against AmerenUE in a 9-3 vote. This was the first stray voltage utility liability verdict in Missouri history. The case established that a utility company could be held liable for neutral current flowing through earth and energizing private dock infrastructure.

A wire for the pool's submersible pump had become pinched near the pool ladder, causing the protective cover to break and exposing bare wire to the water. Swimmers felt "a vibration in the water" before the father yelled to shut the pump off. A 15-year-old boy managed to jump out of the pool once power was cut and heroically rescued his father, sister, and sister's friend. Two of the five victims were unresponsive when EMTs arrived. All five were hospitalized. Police Chief Travis Yike described it as a "freak accident."

# ESD-2025-05-26-1: Electric Shock Incident — Splash in the Boro Waterpark, Statesboro, GA

## Summary

On May 26, 2025 (Memorial Day), approximately 5 patrons including at least 2 children reported feeling electric shocks while in the wave pool at Splash in the Boro Waterpark in Statesboro, Bulloch County, Georgia. The pool was evacuated at approximately 1:30 PM. Statesboro Fire Department responded and classified the incident as "arcing, shorted electrical equipment," identifying a blower unit that potentially shorted out or overheated. EMS evaluated those affected; none were hospitalized. The wave pool was closed and subsequently inspected by 5 licensed electricians and Georgia Power before reopening several days later.

# ESD-2025-07-10-1: Gabriel Gonzalez — Marina Shores, Portage, IN

## Summary

On July 10, 2025, Gabriel Gonzalez, 21, was electrocuted at Marina Shores on Burns Waterway in Portage, Indiana, after diving in to retrieve a cooler.
